submission.natural_language_explanation: Broad previous-token head: predict ordinary English text of three or more words ACTIVE (weakly, about 0.25-0.5 of max, on some ordinary word, whether or not it contains 'how', 'what' or 'both'), and strongly active (0.6-1.0 of max) on the word right after 'how'/'How', 'what', 'both' or, more weakly, 'to'/'To' when that word is what they modify ('how much/many/little/massive', 'what amount', 'both sides', 'to resolve'). The only inactive classes are a single word or interjection with punctuation ('Yes.', 'Indeed.', 'Right?', 'Help!') and bare numeric strings such as decimals, dates, times and prices ('3.14159', '2019-05-12', '11:59 PM', '$25.99'); non-English sentences sit near the line and are not part of the claim.

rival_explanations: Narrow trigger head: only the word right after 'how', 'what', 'both' or 'to' crosses the line, so ordinary English sentences without those words are inactive.

Determiner-modifier head: any word after a determiner, quantifier or degree word ('the', 'that', 'so', 'two', 'many') is as strongly active as after 'how' or 'both', so 'the sides' and 'that much' reach 0.6+ of max like 'both sides' and 'how much'.
